By front running, these individuals or entities can secure better prices and reduce their risk exposure.

Although front running is illegal, detecting and proving it can be challenging for regulatory authorities. In addition, the fast-paced nature of financial markets and the vast amount of data make it difficult to identify instances of front running accurately.

Regulators and exchanges have implemented various measures to prevent front running and protect market integrity. Regulators conduct investigations, impose fines, and pursue legal actions against individuals and institutions found guilty of front running.

The potential for front running can deter investors from participating, leading to decreased liquidity and market efficiency.
